extracted.intended_audience: students, policymakers, and readers interested in public finance and tax policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and practical criteria for designing, assessing, and administering taxes (bases, incidence, administration, and behavioural effects), illustrated by historical examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish ground-rent from building-rent
rubrics_metrics.description: It should not, however, seem very difficult to distinguish those two parts of the rent from one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax designers must separate the part of rent attributable to the land (ground-rent) from that attributable to buildings/improvements (building-rent) when considering taxation on land versus buildings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax houses in same proportion as rent of land (uniform proportionality)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Great Britain the rent of houses is supposed to be taxed in the same proportion as the rent of land, by what is called the annual land tax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where feasible, align rates across similar tax bases (e.g., houses and land) to preserve proportionality; but beware of historical valuation inequalities that make nominal uniformity inequitable in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use stable, public valuations but recognise historical inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: The valuation, according to which each different parish and district is assessed to this tax, is always the same. It was originally extremely unequal, and it still continues to be so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixed historical valuations create administrative simplicity and certainty but may embed persistent inequalities; designers should weigh stability against fairness and consider revaluation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid taxing untenanted property harshly
rubrics_metrics.description: There seems to be a hardship in obliging the proprietor to pay a tax for an untenanted house, from which he can derive no revenue...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxing property not yielding income to its owner is inequitable in many circumstances; consider exemptions or relief for empty properties or methods that account for actual revenue streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revalue on improvement or rebuilding
rubrics_metrics.description: When a house is rebuilt, improved, or enlarged, there is a new valuation, and the tax is rated accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxes tied to property value should be updated when substantial improvements occur so tax base reflects current value; explicit revaluation rules reduce disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer observable proxies to intrusive inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: They have regulated their taxes, therefore, according to some more obvious circumstance...such as the number of hearths or windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When direct measurement of the tax base is difficult or invasive, use observable, countable proxies (e.g., windows, hearths) to estimate liability; this reduces administrative intrusion though it can create distortions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid odious or offensive methods of collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The visit of the tax-gatherer, therefore, was less offensive in [the window tax] than in the hearth-money. The odious visit rendered the tax odious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collection methods that require intrusive searches or inspections (e.g., entering rooms to count hearths) breed popular resentment; choose collection procedures that minimize affront and invasion of privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of highly specific per-unit taxes (window/hearth taxes) causing inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal objection to all such taxes is their inequality; an inequality of the worst kind, as they must frequently fall much heavier upon the poor than upon the rich.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxes levied on counts (windows/hearths) can be regressive and uneven across locales; assess whether the proxy correlates with ability-to-pay and adjust rates or exemptions to prevent disproportionate burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider behavioural responses and long-run price effects (incidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural tendency of the window tax, and of all other taxes upon houses, is to lower rents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxes affect incentives and prices; anticipate whether a tax will reduce supply, lower rents, or otherwise shift incidence to owners, tenants, consumers, or wages, and evaluate who ultimately bears the burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate profit components before taxing (interest vs surplus profit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The revenue or profit arising from stock naturally divides itself into two parts; that which pays the interest...and that surplus part which is over and above what is necessary for paying the interest. This latter part of profit is evidently a subject not taxable directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat the normal compensation for risk/effort (surplus profit) as an appropriate direct tax base, because taxing it undermines the incentive to employ capital; focus on taxing the interest element or design taxes that avoid destroying returns necessary for activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid taxing interest directly when capital is secret or mobile
rubrics_metrics.description: First, the quantity and value of the land which any man possesses, can never be a secret...But the whole amount of the capital stock which he possesses is almost always a secret...Secondly, land is a subject which cannot be removed; whereas stock easily may.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax bases that are invisible or highly mobile are difficult to assess and enforce and may encourage capital flight; prefer immovable or transparent bases, or use indirect methods (e.g., stamps, registration) where direct taxation is impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid severe inquisitions into private circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: An inquisition into every man's private circumstances...would be a source of such continual and endless vexation as no person could support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative systems should minimize invasive scrutiny and complexity; heavy surveillance reduces compliance and may drive away economic activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensate arbitrariness/uncertainty with moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: The extreme inequality and uncertainty of a tax assessed in this manner, can be compensated only by its extreme moderation...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where assessments are inherently imprecise or arbitrary, keep rates low to reduce perceived unfairness and real hardship; moderation mitigates harm from imperfect measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage self-assessment where trust and civic virtue exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Every man assesses himself, and, in the presence of the magistrate, puts annually into the public coffer a certain sum...This tax is generally supposed to be paid with great fidelity. In a small republic...such conscientious and voluntary payment may sometimes be expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-declaration systems can work where social trust and effective civic institutions exist; suitability depends on political culture and enforcement capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise that taxes on particular trades usually fall on consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: A tax, however, upon the profits of stock employed in any particular branch of trade, can never fall finally upon the dealers...but always upon the consumers, who must be obliged to pay in the price of the goods the tax which the dealer advances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When imposing taxes on a specific industry or activity, analyze how competition and demand elasticity will shift the burden (often to consumers) and whether that aligns with policy objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid uniform fixed-amount licences that advantage large operators
rubrics_metrics.description: The tax of twenty shillings a-year for a licence to sell ale...being the same upon all retailers, must necessarily give some advantage to the great, and occasion some oppression to the small dealers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flat per-unit or per-business fees favor large firms and harm small ones; structure licence fees proportionally to scale of activity when equity matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes on agricultural profits tend to reduce rent, not raise prices
rubrics_metrics.description: When a tax is imposed upon the profits of stock employed in agriculture...the final payment of the tax will fall upon the landlord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sectoral differences matter: in agriculture, fixed land use means farmers cannot withdraw capital to raise prices, so taxes reduce rents; policy must consider land-tenure and contract timing (leases) for incidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing profits by observable farming capital induces underinvestment
rubrics_metrics.description: The farmer is commonly assessed in proportion to the stock which he appears to employ...he endeavours to cultivate with the meanest and most wretched instruments...he counterfeits poverty, and wishes to appear scarce able to pay anything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment rules that tie tax to visible inputs encourage concealment and reduced productive investment, harming output and long-term revenue; aim for bases that do not distort productive choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal taxes based on guessed profits (personal taille) are arbitrary and unequal
rubrics_metrics.description: The personal taille...as it is intended to be proportioned to the profits of a certain class of people, which can only be guessed at, is necessarily both arbitrary and unequal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid subjective assessments of ability-to-pay that invite misinformation, favoritism, and corruption; rely on verifiable measures or transparent procedures to allocate burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise public-spirited temporary levies may be payable once but unsustainable if permanent
rubrics_metrics.description: The tax was to be paid but once, in order to relieve the state in a particular exigency...It was, indeed, too heavy to be permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extraordinary, large one-off levies can be collected in moments of public zeal but are generally unsustainable as permanent fiscal measures; design temporary taxes with exit rules and fair sharing of burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate taxes on capital transfers from taxes on revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: While property remains in the possession of the same person...they have never been intended to diminish or take away any part of its capital value, but only some part of the revenue arising from it. But when property changes hands...such taxes have frequently been imposed upon it as necessarily take away some part of its capital value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxes on transfer (inheritance, sale, stamp duties) reduce capital value at the point of transfer and have different equity and behavioural effects than annual taxes on revenue; consider long-term capital effects when imposing transfer taxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use indirect methods (stamps, registration) to tax movable/secret transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: The transference of stock or moveable property...is frequently a secret transaction...It has been taxed indirectly in two different ways; first, by requiring that the deed...should be written upon paper or parchment which had paid a certain stamp duty...secondly, by requiring...that it should be recorded...and by imposing certain duties upon such registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When direct taxation of private or movable transactions is infeasible, use indirect legal formalities (stamps, compulsory registration with duties) to create assessable events without intrusive continual inquiry.
